title: Pipes
summary: Transform how values look in the template without changing the data.
heading: Pipes

blocks.text: A pipe formats a value for display using the | symbol in a template. It only changes what's shown on screen — the underlying data stays exactly the same.
Some pipes take arguments after a colon: {{ value | pipeName:arg1:arg2 }}.
These change the casing of text.

blocks.label: uppercase / lowercase / titlecase
blocks.code:
{{ 'hello' | uppercase }}        <!-- HELLO -->
{{ 'HELLO' | lowercase }}        <!-- hello -->
{{ 'hello world' | titlecase }}  <!-- Hello World -->

blocks.text: Try it — type below and watch the pipes format your text live:
Format numbers as plain decimals, currency, or percentages. The number pipe's argument is 'minIntegerDigits.minFractionDigits-maxFractionDigits'.
Change the amount and see the currency and number pipes reformat it:

blocks.html:
{{ price | currency:'USD' }}

{{ price | number:'1.0-2' }}

blocks.text: date formats a date value. Pass a format string to control how it looks.

blocks.label: date
blocks.code:
{{ today | date }}              <!-- Jun 12, 2026 -->
{{ today | date:'shortTime' }}  <!-- 9:30 AM -->
{{ today | date:'dd/MM/yyyy' }} <!-- 12/06/2026 -->
{{ today | date:'fullDate' }}   <!-- Friday, June 12, 2026 -->

blocks.text: Edit and run — these show today's date in different formats:

blocks.html:
default: {{ today | date }}

time: {{ today | date:'shortTime' }}

full: {{ today | date:'fullDate' }}

blocks.text: json is handy for debugging — it prints any value as JSON. slice takes part of a list or string. keyvalue turns an object into a list you can loop over.

blocks.label: slice (first 3)
keyvalue

blocks.text: Edit and run — see json and slice in action:

blocks.html:
{{ user | json }}

first 3: {{ items | slice:0:3 }}

    @for (item of items | slice:0:3; track item) {
  • {{ item }}
    • }

blocks.text: async unwraps a value that arrives later — a Promise or an Observable — and keeps the screen updated when it changes. It also cleans up the subscription for you.

blocks.label: async

blocks.text: The async pipe pairs perfectly with HttpClient and signals — no manual subscribe/unsubscribe needed.
You can pipe a value through several pipes in a row — they run left to right.
When no built-in pipe fits, write your own. Let the CLI scaffold it for you:

blocks.label: Terminal
blocks.code:
ng generate pipe exclaim
# short version:
ng g p exclaim

blocks.text: A pipe is a class with a transform method, marked with @Pipe.

blocks.label: exclaim.pipe.ts

blocks.text: Pipes are pure by default: they only re-run when their input changes, which keeps them fast. An impure pipe (like async) re-runs more often — use them sparingly.

items: A pipe formats a value for display with | — the data is unchanged.
Arguments come after a colon; chain pipes left to right.
Write your own with @Pipe and a transform method.
